Eagles regain lead in dying minutes , beat New England Patriots to win first Super Bowlhttp : **36;8348;TOOLONG ... src= " https : **33;8386;TOOLONG ... title= " Philadelphia Eagles tight end Zach Ertz ( left ) scores a fourth-quarter touchdown against the New England Patriots in Super Bowl LII on Feb. 4. " alt= " Philadelphia Eagles tight end Zach Ertz ( left ) scores a fourth-quarter touchdown against the New England Patriots in Super Bowl LII on Feb. 4. " data-portal-copyright= " Gregory Shamus " **28;8421;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 77128139 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; MINNEAPOLIS &amp;mdash ; Brady , Shmady. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The greatest , most accomplished quarterback in NFL history put forth another Super Bowl performance for the ages , but this time it wasn&amp;rsquo ; t enough . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the largest explosion of offence in Super Bowl history , the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday night outfought Brady&amp;rsquo ; s New England Patriots , deservedly capturing the Philly franchise&amp;rsquo ; s first Super Bowl championship , 41-33. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Both teams combined for an NFL championship-game record of 1,151 total yards . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This long-elusive Philadelphia victory thrilled most of the decidedly pro-Eagles crowd at the Midwest&amp;rsquo ; s monument to girders and glass , 19-month-old U.S. Bank Stadium . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Eagles hadn&amp;rsquo ; t won an NFL championship since before the Super Bowl era began &amp;mdash ; in 1960 , with a defeat of legendary Vince Lombardi&amp;rsquo ; s Green Bay Packers . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Now , they&amp;rsquo ; ve got their first Vince Lombardi Trophy &amp;mdash ; given annually to the Super Bowl champion . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Quarterback Nick ( Nick Who ? ) Foles was named MVP of Super Bowl LII . He headed the list of offensive heroes for the Eagles&amp;rsquo ; unstoppable offence . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We have such a great group of guys , &amp;rdquo ; Foles told NBC on the euphoric post-game champion&amp;rsquo ; s podium , only about 10 yards from where his tight end , Zach Ertz , caught his game-winning touchdown throw with 2:21 left . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That was Foles&amp;rsquo ; third touchdown pass of the game . Inexplicably , in just his fourth career playoff game , and only his sixth start since the Eagles&amp;rsquo ; superstar second-year QB Carson Wentz was lost for the season on Dec. 10 with a blown-out knee , Foles played superbly , matching Brady clutch throw for clutch throw throughout , if not yard for yard . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Brady threw for three touchdowns without an interception and 505 yards . The latter mark broke the single-game Super Bowl record he set just a year ago , 466. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Foles , a sixth-year pro in his second stint with the Eagles , threw a few unwise passes in this gigantic indoor stadium , and got away with perhaps more than his share . But on third downs and , especially , on New England&amp;rsquo ; s side of the field he performed spectacularly . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; To be part of this organization , to be in this moment is something you dream about as a kid , &amp;rdquo ; Foles said . &amp;ldquo ; To be right here with the confetti flying with the greatest group of men &amp;hellip ; &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As for long-suffering Philadelphians ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We have been wanting this for a long time , &amp;rdquo ; Foles said , &amp;ldquo ; and I am just blessed to be a part of it . We have such a great group of guys . Such a great city to play for and I am proud to be a Philadelphia Eagle . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Foles finished 28-of-43 for 373 yards , three touchdowns and only one interception . He also caught a touchdown pass on probably the greatest goal-line call in Super Bowl history , a play sure to go down in NFL lore . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; With 34 seconds left before halftime , on 4th-and goal from the one , Eagles head coach Doug Pederson went for it . He had Foles line up in the pistol ( the short shotgun ) with third-string running back Corey Clement behind him . Then Foles repositioned himself as a wingback to the right . Clement took the direct snap , ran to his left , and handed off to backup tight end Trey Burton on an end-around back to the right . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Burton then slowed down and threw a pass to a wide-open Foles , who&amp;rsquo ; d filtered out into the right flat of the end zone , uncovered . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The quarterback caught the pass for a startlingly cool touchdown. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I hadn&amp;rsquo ; t thrown a touchdown pass since high school , &amp;rdquo ; Burton said in the incredibly jubilant Eagles locker room . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Eagles never trailed until Brady hit his trusted tight end , Rob Gronkowski , with a four-yard corner lob with 9:22 left . That gave New England a 33-32 lead , after earlier trailing as much as 15-3 and 22-12 in the second quarter , and 29-19 in the third . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Foles showed steel-spine courage , though , in rallying the Eagles &amp;ndash ; on what surely will be remembered as the greatest drive in franchise history &amp;ndash ; to what proved to be the winning touchdown with 2:21 left . Foles hit tight end Zach Ertz on an 11-yard scoring slant . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Up 38-33 , the Eagles went for two and didn&amp;rsquo ; t get it . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It didn&amp;rsquo ; t matter . One play after the kickoff , following an eight-yard completion to Gronkowski , Brady was stripped of the ball by fellow University of Michigan alum Brandon Graham , Philadelphia&amp;rsquo ; s leading sacker in the regular season . Rookie defensive end Derek Barnett recovered the ball at the New England 33 , with 2:09 left . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; After three running plays the Eagles went up 41-33 on Jake Elliott&amp;rsquo ; s 46-yard field goal , with 1:05 left . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Brady passed the Patriots from his own nine only as far as midfield in the dying seconds . After his Hail Mary heave on the game&amp;rsquo ; s last play fell incomplete in the Philly end zone , it was over . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Canons sounded , and the green-and-white confetti machines went to work . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Before the end of the third quarter the offences combined for the most total yards in the 52-year history of the Super Bowl . Philly finished with 538 , New England with 613. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Both defences performed awfully in the first half , mailing it in almost as much as Justin Timberlake did at halftime . Alas , defences can not pre-record their performances , as it sounded like JT did . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Defenders got gashed again in the second half . They left receivers wide open all over the field , flailed meekly at tackle attempts ( ProFootballFocus.com counted 10 by the Patriots alone ) and made just about every offensive performer look like an all-pro. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But credit each team&amp;rsquo ; s offensive play-callers : Pats offensive co-ordinator Josh McDaniels and Eagles head coach and chief offensive strategist , Pederson . Both called masterful games . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Although Brady threw for a startling 267 yards in the first half alone , Foles nearly matched him &amp;ndash ; completing 13-of-22 for 215 yards and a touchdown. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The first-half offensive fireworks immediately continued following the elongated halftime break . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Each team scored a touchdown on its opening possession , as Brady and Foles kept throwing darts into open receivers&amp;rsquo ; hands . " alt= " New England Patriots quarterback Tom Brady celebrates his team 's win in the AFC Championship Game on Jan. 21. " data-portal-copyright= " Maddie Meyer " **28;9083;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 77122019 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; On Jan. 23 , Sports Illustrated posted the following tweet , which got us thinking . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;blockquote class= " twitter-tweet " data-width= " 550 " data-dnt= " true " &gt;&lt;p lang= " en " dir= " ltr " &gt;Fourteen years ago , a 7-year-old in Foxboro told Tom Brady he had named his baby brother after him . ' He was pretty young then . It 's probably something he hears once or twice a week now . ' &lt;a href= " https : //t.co/VDHRoyxxsQ " &gt;https : //t.c ... -- Sports Illustrated ( @SInow ) &lt;a href= " https : **33;9113;TOOLONG ... 23 , **33;9148;TOOLONG &lt;script async src= " https : **33;9183;TOOLONG " charset= " utf-8 " &gt;&lt;/script&gt; &lt;p&gt; Just how many babies get named after Super Bowl-winning quarterbacks ? If there are three things America loves , it&amp;rsquo ; s the Super Bowl , quarterbacks and babies . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The U.S. government offers &lt;a href= " https : **33;9218;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;baby name data&lt;/a&gt; &amp;nbsp ; taken from Social Security applications , broken down by state and going back to 1901. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In Massachusetts , the name &amp;ldquo ; Brady&amp;rdquo ; appears in the data only four times prior to 1990 , accounting for 35 applications . It appears every year from 1990 on , but was used only 153 times in the 1990s. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Below is a chart showing the usage of the names Thomas and Brady in Massachusetts since Tom Brady was drafted by the Patriots in the sixth round in 2000 . For the purposes of these charts , we are labelling the years teams appeared in the Super Bowl . The Patriots appeared in XXXVI on Feb. 3 , 2002 following the 2001 NFL season , so 2002 is the labelled year . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **33;9253;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;9288;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Brady&amp;rdquo ; remains low in 2000 and 2001 , but it shoots up to 90 in 2002 after Brady replaced Drew Bledsoe and won his first Super Bowl . It moved up slightly in 2003 , then rose 65 per cent after the second victory at the start of 2004 . Another win in 2005 brought it closer to 200 and 49th overall among boys names in the state . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In 2007 , the season the Patriots put together their undefeated regular season , the name Brady broke through the 200 level and was ranked 34th . This was the Brady heyday . It has been in decline since then , falling to 50th in 2008 . By 2010 , Brady was no longer in triple digits , and it has remained relatively static through 2016 regardless of the Patriots&amp;rsquo ; fortunes . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The name Thomas , however , has rebounded over the last three years available after a long , slow decline . It was the 17th-ranked name for boys in 2016. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Are we able to find similar results for other quarterback names in other states ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Looking at Bens and Benjamins in Pennsylvania has no value because the name is popular on its own . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Below is a chart for Russells in Washington state . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **33;9318;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;9353;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; The name Russell reached its peak in Washington after the Second World War , but dwindled back into the 10s and 20s by the mid-1990s . But the name has enjoyed a modest renaissance , reaching 50 in 2014 , the year Russell Wilson led the Seahawks to the win in Super Bowl XLVII against Denver . Another 44 boys received the name in 2015 , showing prospective parents blamed Pete Carroll rather than Wilson for the interception at the goal line to end the game . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The name Peyton offers an interesting case in two states . Here&amp;rsquo ; s a chart&amp;nbsp ; reflecting Peyton Manning&amp;rsquo ; s long tenure in Indiana . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **33;9383;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;9418;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; The name Peyton doesn&amp;rsquo ; t even show up in the data until 1992 and it isn&amp;rsquo ; t until 1998 , the year Manning was drafted , that it becomes more common as a boy&amp;rsquo ; s name . The usage for boys peaks in 2006 , the year Manning led the Colts to their first Super Bowl victory since moving from Baltimore in 1984 . Female Peytons outnumber males again starting in 2011 , the year Manning sat out recovering from neck surgery before leaving the organization . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Now let&amp;rsquo ; s look at whether Peyton became a thing in Colorado . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **33;9448;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;9483;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; It did not , despite Super Bowl appearances in 2014 and 2016. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Now comes the quarterback with perhaps the most interesting effect on baby naming in two states . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **33;9513;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;9548;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; We limited the scope here just to the name Eli rather than extend it to other forms of the name . Elijah would be a more common long form , but Eli Manning&amp;rsquo ; s given name is Elisha. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Eli receives a bit of a bump in New York state following Manning&amp;rsquo ; s draft in 2004 . It spikes in New York in 2006 , the year of Manning&amp;rsquo ; s first Super Bowl win . It continues to rise , though , which may indicate a general interest in the name apart from Manning . Or it could reflect the popularity of the Giants ; it&amp;rsquo ; s hard to tell . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; We do see another rise following the 2012 Super Bowl win and continued strength of the name . But is it all Eli Manning ? Or is it because many babies look like Eli Manning , sort of nondescript and mushy with strange expressions we can&amp;rsquo ; t read ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **33;9578;TOOLONG ... title= " New York Giants quarterback Eli Manning stands on the sidelines against the Arizona Cardinals on Dec. 24 , 2017. " alt= " Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Nick Foles celebrates a touchdown against the Minnesota Vikings in the NFC Championship Game on Jan. 21. " data-portal-copyright= " Patrick Smith " **28;11167;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 77119667 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Eagles&amp;rsquo ; Nick Foles is attempting to become the eighth backup quarterback to play a significant playoff role on a team that wins the Super Bowl . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Foles took over as the starter in Week 15 after Carson Wentz tore his ACL against the Rams . Since then has thrown for 1,037 yards in five starts , including playoff wins over Atlanta and Minnesota . Philadelphia , which might have expected its hold on the top seed in the NFC could be in jeopardy without Wentz , has not missed a beat . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Foles&amp;rsquo ; exploits bring to mind names from the past like Jeff Hostetler , the Giants quarterback who saved the season in 1990 by going on a five-game run in place of an injured Phil Simms , culminating in a 20-19 win over Buffalo in Super Bowl XXV. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Below are two charts showing the playoff passing yards and the playoff quarterback rating for each player in his Super Bowl run . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **33;11197;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;11232;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **33;11262;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;11297;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Not everyone of the players on the list below were late-season heroes . Let&amp;rsquo ; s examine the players and their circumstances . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Earl Morrall&lt;/strong&gt; : The career backup from Muskegon , Mich. , played 21 seasons in the NFL yet only had four years in which he started more than 10 games . He was , perhaps , the greatest backup in the history of the league , especially late in his career when he saved seasons for both the Baltimore Colts and the Miami Dolphins . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In 1968 , Morrall had already been in the league 13 years when he joined the Colts and was thrust into the leading role because of a pre-season injury to Johnny Unitas . Morrell&amp;rsquo ; s Colts compiled a 13-1 record and won the NFL championship game , but suffered the first great upset in Super Bowl history at the hands of Joe Namath and the New York Jets . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Morrall replaced Unitas in Super Bowl V after the starter bruised his ribs in the second quarter against Dallas . Baltimore , now in the AFC after the leagues merged , trailed 13-6 when Morrall entered the game for the last series before halftime . The Colts benefited from two interceptions of Craig Morton deep in Cowboys territory that led to 10 points , including Jim O&amp;rsquo ; Brien&amp;rsquo ; s 32-yard field goal with nine seconds left in the game . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; When head coach Don Shula left Baltimore for Miami , he didn&amp;rsquo ; t hesitate to add Morrall to the roster for the 1972 season . Starter Bob Griese was injured in Game 5 and Morrall led the Dolphins the rest of the way to their perfect 14-0 regular season . Morrall started the first two playoff games but gave way to Griese in the Super Bowl , which Miami won 14-7 over Washington to cap the league&amp;rsquo ; s only completely perfect season . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Jim Plunkett&lt;/strong&gt; : He resurrected his career in 1980 after eight mostly mediocre seasons in New England and San Francisco . He joined the Raiders in 1979 and was asked to take over from an ineffective Dan Pastorini in Week 5 . Oakland won nine of their last 11 regular-season games and Plunkett helped them become the first wild-card team to win the Super Bowl . He threw three touchdown passes , including one of 80 yards to Kenny King to defeat Philadelphia 27-10. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Doug Williams&lt;/strong&gt; : After a two-year stint in the USFL , Williams returned to the NFL with Washington to back up Jay Schroeder . Williams only started two games in 1987 , both losses , but came off the bench in three others , including the season finale , all wins . Head coach Joe Gibbs went with Williams as the playoff starter and he reeled off three straight wins , including a 42-10 crushing of Denver in Super Bowl XXII . Williams , the first black quarterback to start an NFL title game , threw four second-quarter touchdown passes to bury the Broncos by halftime . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;span class= " embed-youtube " style= " text-align:center ; display : block ; " &gt;&lt;iframe class='youtube-player ' type='text/html ' width= ' 640 ' height= ' 390 ' src='https : **34;11327;TOOLONG ... allowfullscreen='true ' style='border:0 ; ' **28;11363;TOOLONG ... &lt;strong&gt;Jeff Hostetler&lt;/strong&gt; : He had been a backup in New York for five seasons and was contemplating retirement late in the 1990 season when he came in to replace Simms , who had a foot injury , in the second-last game of the season . The Giants won their final two regular-season games to finish 13-3 . Hostetler was injured himself in the NFC championship game against the 49ers , but he came back later to lead two scoring drives in the 15-13 win . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In Super Bowl XXV against Buffalo , which was making the first of its four straight appearances in the big game , Hostetler threw a second-quarter touchdown pass and had four completions on the fourth-quarter drive that led to Matt Bahr&amp;rsquo ; s field goal . He then turned the one-point lead over to the defence and the bedeviled Scott Norwood&amp;rsquo ; s right foot . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;span class= " embed-youtube " style= " text-align:center ; display : block ; " &gt;&lt;iframe class='youtube-player ' type='text/html ' width= ' 640 ' height= ' 390 ' src='https : **34;11393;TOOLONG ... allowfullscreen='true ' style='border:0 ; ' **28;11429;TOOLONG ... &lt;strong&gt;Kurt Warner&lt;/strong&gt; : His path through the Arena Football League and NFL Europe is well told , leading Warner to be Trent Green&amp;rsquo ; s untested backup in 1999 . Green tore an ACL in a pre-season game , Warner was thrust into the spotlight and a Hall of Fame career was born . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Rams offence under Warner became known as the Greatest Show on Turf . Warner was the league MVP , leading the Rams to a 13-3 record . He is far and away the leader among our championship backups with 1,063 passing yards and the only one with a playoff passer rating of 100 . And yet the Rams still could have gone home empty-handed from Super Bowl XXXIV had linebacker Mike Jones not tackled Titans receiver Kevin Dyson on the one-yard line to end the game . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;span class= " embed-youtube " style= " text-align:center ; display : block ; " &gt;&lt;iframe class='youtube-player ' type='text/html ' width= ' 640 ' height= ' 390 ' src='https : **34;11459;TOOLONG ... allowfullscreen='true ' style='border:0 ; ' **28;11495;TOOLONG ... &lt;strong&gt;Trent Dilfer&lt;/strong&gt; : The Ravens quarterback remains a punchline among some fans who decry his anemic performances on the way to Baltimore&amp;rsquo ; s win in Super Bowl XXXV . " data-portal-copyright= " Jessica Hill " **28;13717;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 77107872 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Vince McMahon is bringing back the XFL . It&amp;rsquo ; s just like the old saying goes : If at first you don&amp;rsquo ; t succeed , wait 20 years and then try again , but this time do a lot of things the exact opposite of the way you tried them the first time . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That may not be exactly how the saying goes . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There was a point a couple of months ago , when rumours first started that McMahon , the wildly rich wrestling impresario , was going to restart his failed football venture , that you could at least squint at it a certain way and get a sense of what he was trying to do . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The National Football League has had some TV-ratings problems of late , and it has had the long-running controversy over certain players kneeling during the national anthem , and some people think the sport is ruining itself by trying to eliminate dangerous hits . As it happens , the President of the United States has criticized the NFL for all of those things . McMahon&amp;rsquo ; s wife , Linda , is in the Trump cabinet . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In that light , you could see where McMahon might have been headed . The original XFL , which launched in 2001 and also died in 2001 , was infamously pro-violence . There were no fair catches on punts , and the coin toss was replaced with an opening tussle for the ball ( seriously ! ) , and there was a general vibe that this was FOOTBALL , dammit . The links to McMahon&amp;rsquo ; s wrestling business were overt , and you got the sense that if he could figure out a way to allow the football players to brain each other with a steel chair , he would have done it . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; So it was reasonable to assume that the new XFL would have tried to recapture some of that : A wilder league for football fans who , like Donald Trump , think the NFL has gone soft . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Instead , McMahon announced on Thursday that the XFL , which would begin play in 2020 with eight teams and a 10-game schedule , would be football &amp;ldquo ; re-imagined. &amp;rdquo ; The imagination part , oddly , is mostly still to come . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; On a conference call with media , McMahon said the main goal of the XFL is &amp;ldquo ; to give football back to fans . &amp;rdquo ; If you can figure out what that means , you are ahead of me . The WWE boss said it would be a safer version of football , where medical expertise would be sought , but he also said it would be faster-paced , and the sizzle-reel video that launched on Thursday also promised &amp;ldquo ; fewer infractions. &amp;rdquo ; McMahon also said that one of the ideas under consideration is no halftime period , in an effort to speed up the game to a tidy two hours . So : fewer penalties , and no rest and recovery at halftime , but also &amp;hellip ; safer ? These things seem hard to square . Are the games going to be played in a bouncy castle ? A giant ball pit ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **33;13747;TOOLONG ... title= " Eighteen years ago , Vince McMahon was announcing the first XFL , which expired shortly after its inaugural season in 2001. " alt= " Eighteen years ago , Vince McMahon was announcing the first XFL , which expired shortly after its inaugural season in 2001. " data-portal-copyright= " Ezio Petersen " **28;13782;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 77107875 " /&gt; &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;13812;TOOLONG ... failed miserably after just one season in 2001 , but WWE 's Vince McMahon is bringing back the **35;13848;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; Where the original XFL was a joint venture with the broadcaster NBC , which bailed after one season because the ratings had tanked , McMahon says he is going alone on this . He&amp;rsquo ; s investing US$100 million of his own money in the new XFL , and his new company Alpha Entertainment will own all the franchises and set all the rules , likely including one that will require players to stand during the national anthem . Asked on the conference call what kinds of opportunities there would be for crossovers between the WWE and XFL , McMahon said none whatsoever . This time , he&amp;rsquo ; s keeping the football business totally separate , an indication that if the XFL ends up being the equivalent of McMahon setting $100 million on fire , the WWE won&amp;rsquo ; t be caught up in the conflagration . Oh , and where the first XFL played up the sex appeal of cheerleaders &amp;mdash ; NBC&amp;rsquo ; s own Bob Costas called it a cross between high-school football and a &amp;ldquo ; tawdry strip club&amp;rdquo ; &amp;mdash ; this one , McMahon says , will be &amp;ldquo ; family friendly . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It is all very puzzling . It is true that , as McMahon said , the media landscape is vastly different now and an upstart league wouldn&amp;rsquo ; t necessarily need a big network TV deal to survive , but it will need some way to make money from viewership . How eager would Amazon or Facebook be to buy up the streaming rights of the successor to a football league that McMahon himself once called a &amp;ldquo ; colossal failure&amp;rdquo ; ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A conspiracy theorist might imagine that , despite McMahon&amp;rsquo ; s milquetoast pronouncements on Thursday , he really does intend the new XFL to be everything the NFL is not . More head shots , no late hits , no anthem kneeling and maybe every once in a while someone has to wrestle a bear . Part of the reason for the long runway before a game is played , he said , is so the XFL can hear from fans about what they want . Does he hope that middle America will tell him what he wants to hear ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It sounds , admittedly , like a crazy plan . New England&amp;rsquo ; s victories are noted in blue . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **33;14538;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;14573;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; It happens that 30 of the 96 conference champions were outgained by their opponent , ranging from the minus-2 differential for the 2010 Steelers to minus-218 for the 2009 Saints . Seventeen teams have been outgained by 50 or more yards and four by 100 or more . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Patriots have split their 10 AFC title games evenly . The four previous Patriots team with a negative differential split their Super Bowls 2-2 . New England is 3-2 in the five Super Bowls in which they had a positive differential in the conference title game . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Philadelphia Eagles have had a positive differential of more than 100 yards in all three of their winning conference title games and lost their two previous Super Bowls . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There are no omens lurking here . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Photo of the day&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; No. 1 seeds and 13-3 teams are rarely considered underdogs in the NFL playoffs , but the Eagles have widely been viewed as such ever since Carson Wentz tore his ACL in Week 14 . For Pyeongchang , TLN will show one hockey game a day ( men&amp;rsquo ; s and women&amp;rsquo ; s ) in both languages , as well as primetime encore broadcasts and highlights . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Nutritional analysis&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **33;15354;TOOLONG ... title= " Minnesota Vikings quarterback Case Keenum celebrates a playoff win over the New Orleans Saints on Jan. 14. " alt= " Minnesota Vikings quarterback Case Keenum celebrates a playoff win over the New Orleans Saints on Jan. 14. " data-portal-copyright= " Jamie Squire " **28;15389;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 77084271 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Social media was still buzzing this morning about the Vikings&amp;rsquo ; astonishing and unlikely last-play victory over the Saints on Sunday . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The win allowed Minnesota to become the first team to advance past the division round for a chance to play the Super Bowl in the stadium where they play their regular-season home games . This weekend , the Vikings will travel to Philadelphia , where a win against the Eagles will mean playing Super Bowl LII back home at US Bank Stadium on Feb. 4. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It seemed worth looking into the circumstances around the first seven attempts . But it didn&amp;rsquo ; t take long to realize the whole story was riding the thin edge of a strict definition of what &amp;ldquo ; home&amp;rdquo ; means . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The whole narrative falls apart while looking at Super Bowl XI , the game played at the Rose Bowl in Pasadena , Calif. , to decide the champion of the 1976 NFL season . It turns out that maybe there were actually 12 teams with a chance to play the Super Bowl at home , if &amp;ldquo ; home&amp;rdquo ; means home market rather than home stadium . And three of those extra four teams not only got to the conference championship , two went to the Super Bowl and one of them won . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The NFL and broadcasters are pressing a strict definition of &amp;ldquo ; home&amp;rdquo ; meaning home stadium to add drama to Minnesota&amp;rsquo ; s push . And really , the whole thing is sort of dumb since most NFL franchises have never had the opportunity to host a Super Bowl , leaving this distinction to be fought over primarily by a handful of teams in the south and west and teams like Minnesota with domes. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Below is a map showing the locations of the eight teams that had a chance to play the Super Bowl in their home stadium ( indicated by the numbers ) and the four who had a chance to play in a stadium within their home market ( indicated by the letters ) . Below the map are annotation for each number and letter . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **33;15419;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;15454;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;1,2 : Miami Dolphins ( Super Bowl V and XIII ) &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Super Bowl V , to conclude the 1970 season , was already the third Super Bowl to be played at the Orange Bowl in Miami . But it was the first time the Dolphins had made the playoffs after four fruitless seasons in the AFL before the merger with the NFL . It was legendary Dolphins coach Don Shula&amp;rsquo ; s first season in Miami after seven season in Baltimore . But Miami , which finished 10-4 in the regular season and earned the AFC wild-card spot , fell 21-14 against Oakland , which was 8-4-2 but earned the home game because it was a division winner . Shula&amp;rsquo ; s former team , the Colts , went on to win the Super Bowl over Dallas . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Dolphins didn&amp;rsquo ; t make the playoffs the next time the Super Bowl was at the Orange Bowl , following the 1975 season , but they rose to the occasion the next time , following the 1978 season . However , Miami didn&amp;rsquo ; t make it past the wild-card round despite an 11-5 record . They turned the ball over five times and lost 17-9 at home to the Houston Oilers. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;3,4 : Miami Dolphins ( Super Bowl XXIX and XXXIII ) &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The next opportunity for a home-stadium Super Bowl didn&amp;rsquo ; t come until 16 years later , again with the Dolphins . Now playing at Joe Robbie Stadium in Miami Gardens , Fla. , the Dolphins made it to the division round following the 1994 season but blew a 21-6 halftime lead in San Diego to lose 22-21. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Four years after that , the Dolphins had their final opportunity . Miami was only a wild-card team and , after getting past Buffalo in the first round , was destroyed 38-3 in Denver as Terrell Davis ran for 199 yards . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;5 : Tampa Bay Buccaneers ( Super Bowl XXXV ) &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This was the third Super Bowl in Tampa but the first at Raymond James Stadium . The 2000 season was the middle of just the second period of sustained success for the mostly sad-sack Bucs , who had now made the playoffs in three of four seasons for head coach Tony Dungy . But after making the conference final the season before , Tampa Bay was held to only 199 yards of offence in a 21-3 loss at Philadelphia in the wild-card round . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;6 : Arizona Cardinals ( Super Bowl XLIX ) &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It was another 14 seasons before the Cardinals had the next chance . It took an 11-5 record to earn a wild-card berth in the 2014 season , yet the Cardinals had to travel to Carolina to play the Panthers , who were a division winner with a 7-8-1 record . Arizona had a 14-13 halftime lead but was shut out in the second half , save for a meaningless safety Carolina conceded with three seconds left . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;7 : Houston Texans ( Super Bowl LI ) &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Last season , Houston was getting its first Super Bowl in 13 years and the Texans made the playoffs for the second straight season . After beating Oakland in the wild-card round , Houston had to travel to New England for the division round . They trailed the Patriots 17-13 at halftime but were unable to score more than a field goal in the second half , and lost 34-16 . New England travelled to Houston three weeks later to stage the greatest comeback victory in Super Bowl history . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;8 : Minnesota Vikings ( Super Bowl LII ) &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;blockquote class= " twitter-tweet " data-width= " 550 " data-dnt= " true " &gt;&lt;p lang= " en " dir= " ltr " &gt; ? ? &lt;a href= " https : **33;15484;TOOLONG ... Sideline Cam&lt;a href= " https : **33;15519;TOOLONG ... &lt;a href= " https : //t.co/fRe9CZTlwt " &gt;pic.twitter ... -- Minnesota Vikings ( @Vikings ) &lt;a href= " https : **33;15554;TOOLONG ... 15 , **33;15589;TOOLONG &lt;script async src= " https : **33;15624;TOOLONG " charset= " utf-8 " &gt;&lt;/script&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;A , B , D : Los Angeles Rams ( Super Bowl XI , XIV and XXI ) &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Verison 1.0 of the L.A. Rams made the playoffs in three of the five seasons the Super Bowl was played at the Rose Bowl in nearby Pasadena , Calif . The Rams played at the L.A. Coliseum through 1979 and were out in Anaheim from 1980-94 while keeping the Los Angeles affiliation . The Rose Bowl is only 23 kilometres from the Coliseum . New Era Field , home of the Bills , is nearly 20 kilometres from downtown Buffalo . You can easily drive a 23-kilometre straight line and never leave the city of Calgary . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The 1976 Rams made the conference championship game , losing 24-13 to Minnesota . The 1984 49ers finished the season 15-1 , losing only in Pittsburgh in Week 7 , and rolled to the title game allowing only 10 points to the Giants in the division round and shutting out the Bears in the conference final . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the Super Bowl &amp;mdash ; played about 50 kilometres from their home stadium at Candlestick Park , but well within the Bay Area &amp;mdash ; &amp;nbsp ; the 49ers earned their second rings with a 38-16 win over Miami . It seemed worth investigating how likely it is Gruden could finish the whole 10 years . There have been a few decades-long head coaching tenures in the NFL , but they are rare . How often has one head coach lasted 10 or more years with one team in one continuous stretch ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Below is a histogram showing the number and the percentage of head coaches broken into two-year increments , regardless of the number of teams he&amp;rsquo ; s worked for . The first bar shows the head coaches who have been the sideline boss for a total of 1-2 years , then 3-4 years , 5-6 years , and so on up to George Halas&amp;rsquo ; s 40 years with the Bears ( of whom he also happened to be the owner ) . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **33;16867;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;16902;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Only 13.9 per cent of the 489 head coaches in the AFL and NFL have lasted 10 years or more . Gruden already has 11 years under his belt , four with the Raiders from 1998-2001 and seven with the Buccaneers from 2002-08 . He&amp;rsquo ; s already beaten those odds . To become a 20-year man , he would join a list of only 15 men that includes Don Shula and Curly Lambeau ( 33 years ) , Tom Landry ( 29 years ) , Bill Belichick ( 23 years and counting ) , and Chuck Noll and Dan Reeves ( 23 years ) . Andy Reid will hit 20 years next season . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Of the 68 head coaches who have had careers of 10 or more years , only 33 managed to have a tenure with one one team that lasted for 10 or more years . Below is a chart of those tenures , sorted from earliest to most recent . Incredibly , there are six coaches currently compiling one of these long-term assignments . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **33;16932;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;16967;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; We&amp;rsquo ; re including the Saints&amp;rsquo ; Sean Payton , even though his tenure is bisected by his 2012 suspension from the Bountygate investigation . We won&amp;rsquo ; t credit him for the year he sat out , but we&amp;rsquo ; ll give him credit for an unbroken term of employment . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s interesting that Halas was head coach for 40 seasons , but that they came in four 10-year increments . He was a owner-player-coach in the first segment , and he returned the bench for the second instalment to save money during the Depression . His third stint came after he served in the Navy . His fourth period lasted until the beginning of the Super Bowl era. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Finally , let&amp;rsquo ; s look at the Raiders&amp;rsquo ; history , with a chart that shows their wins each season , labels the three Super Bowl-winning seasons and marks the four periods in which the head coach lasted at least as long as Gruden&amp;rsquo ; s first four-year tenure . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **33;16997;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;17032;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; John Madden and Tom Flores are easily the two most successful coaches in team history , which spans 21 head coaches . It happened Sunday at EverBank Field , when the host Jacksonville Jaguars eked past the Buffalo Bills in the second AFC wild-card game of the weekend . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Ugly ? Odoriferous ? Sure . But so what , said Jaguars cornerback Jalen Ramsey , whose interception near mid-field with 26 seconds left sealed the Jaguars&amp;rsquo ; first playoff victory in exactly 10 years , less two days . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Yeah , I don&amp;rsquo ; t care what people call it , &amp;rdquo ; Ramsey said . &amp;ldquo ; We&amp;rsquo ; re going to come in here for another week , while other teams are sitting home . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; True enough . Twenty-four teams , to be exact . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But , oh , that woeful quarterbacking on Sunday . Jacksonville&amp;rsquo ; s Blake Bortles was so awful , aerially , he was able to complete a pass to only one wide receiver all day &amp;mdash ; backup Dede Westbrook . He had five catches for 48 yards . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Bortles actually rushed for more yards ( 88 ) on impromptu scrambles than he passed for ( 87 , on 12-of-23 throwing ) . Time and again in the first half , Bortles badly missed simple short throws , mostly screens . Perhaps that&amp;rsquo ; s why in the second half he chose to scramble so often &amp;mdash ; eight times for 53 yards . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; He&amp;rsquo ; s an athlete , that&amp;rsquo ; s what that tells me , &amp;rdquo ; Jaguars left tackle Cam Robinson said . &amp;ldquo ; He&amp;rsquo ; s going to go out there and do whatever it takes for us to win . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Bortles&amp;rsquo ; scrambles proved the difference , because the Bills defence successfully blanketed the Jags&amp;rsquo ; sensational rookie running back Leonard Fournette , holding him to just 57 yards on 21 carries . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Bortles scrambled three times for 20 yards on the game&amp;rsquo ; s only ( and decisive ) touchdown drive late in the third quarter , a march that covered 86 yards in 15 plays and chewed 8:52 off the clock . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Those quarterback runs really hurt us , &amp;rdquo ; Bills linebacker Preston Brown said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Bortles capped the drive with a 4th-and-goal play-action TD pass from the Buffalo one-yard line , to backup tight end Ben Koyack. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Thereafter , the Bills offence never advanced further than Jacksonville&amp;rsquo ; s 38. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The defence came back and did a heck of a job in the second half , &amp;rdquo ; Jaguars head coach Doug Marrone said . &amp;ldquo ; Playoff football is about you just going out there to win . But he was dreadful thereafter , completing 6-of-16 for 44 yards until getting knocked out ( perhaps literally , briefly ) on a wicked but legal hit with 1:17 left . That came on Buffalo&amp;rsquo ; s last , desperation drive to try to tie or win the game . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Backup Bills QB Nathan Peterman finished up , and although he scrambled for a drive-extending first down on 4th-and-3 , then hit receiver Deonte Thompson for 14 yards on a deepish curl to the Jaguars&amp;rsquo ; 38 , he was flagged for intentional grounding , then threw the hope-ending pick . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But this one&amp;rsquo ; s on Taylor . That&amp;rsquo ; s unacceptably bad quarterbacking at the NFL level , when your team needs you most . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Will the Bills bring him back ? " data-portal-copyright= " Chris Young " **28;22842;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 77048999 " /&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Nutritional analysis&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; Early in the tenure of Raptors coach Dwane Casey , he used to tell reporters that his goal for team defence was to hold opponents below 43 per cent shooting . As it turned out , that was a worthy goal in his first season , 2011-12 , when the Raptors held opponents to 43.5 per cent shooting . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The closest they&amp;rsquo ; ve come since then is 44.4 per cent in 2015-16 , although Casey&amp;rsquo ; s target may have changed as his teams became offensive powerhouses and as the league evolved into trying to shoot as much as it could from the paint and from beyond the three-point line . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Last night&amp;rsquo ; s dismal 98-93 loss in Dallas was beyond weird for the number of times the teams traded scoring runs , alternating wildly between being hot and cold . The Mavericks , in fact , shot only 42.6 per cent . The Raptors could only manage to shoot 33.7 per cent . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Below are a couple of charts showing how the Raptors&amp;rsquo ; offensive and defensive shooting percentages have evolved over Casey&amp;rsquo ; s seven seasons . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;22872;TOOLONG ... class= " aligncenter size-full wp-image-77048973 " src= " https : **33;22907;TOOLONG ... alt= " " width= " 640 " height= " 600 " srcset= " https : **31;22942;TOOLONG ... 640w , https : **39;22975;TOOLONG ... 150w , https : **39;23016;TOOLONG ... 300w " sizes= " ( max-width : 640px ) 100vw , 640px " &gt;&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;23057;TOOLONG ... class= " aligncenter size-full wp-image-77048972 " src= " https : **33;23092;TOOLONG ... alt= " " width= " 640 " height= " 600 " srcset= " https : **31;23127;TOOLONG ... 640w , https : **39;23160;TOOLONG ... 150w , https : **39;23201;TOOLONG ... 300w " sizes= " ( max-width : 640px ) 100vw , 640px " &gt;&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Toronto&amp;rsquo ; s 47.4 per cent shooting this season ranks seventh in the league ; last season&amp;rsquo ; s 46.4 mark was 11th . On defence , oddly , they rank 25th in both seasons with identical 44.9 marks . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The box plots above show the range of the Raptors per-game shooting percentages , with the box representing the range between the 25th and 75th percentile and the line in the middle of the box showing the median . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Although the Raptors haven&amp;rsquo ; t moved the needle on their overall defensive percentage in the last two seasons , the spread between the offensive and defensive medians is at its highest level in Casey&amp;rsquo ; s seven seasons . " data-portal-copyright= " Eric Espada " **28;27167;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 77020004 " /&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Nutritional analysis&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; Baseball&amp;rsquo ; s Winter Meetings kicked off Sunday in Orlando , which means the off-season is ready to begin in earnest . General managers and agents will be in one place and the movement of free agents can now start to shape rosters for the 2018 season . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Anecdotally , it seemed like the off-season was off to a slow start . As fans have become more invested in team-building machinations , the off-season has gained a brighter spotlight and it seemed like there was a dearth of movement once the World Series ended , qualifying offers were sorted out and teams knew which players were on the market . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Sunday started the beginning of week 50 on the 2017 calendar . From the start of week 45 on Nov. 5 , there were only five major-league free-agent signings , the first of which didn&amp;rsquo ; t come until Nov. 20 . Only two of those five players had any sort of name recognition : the White Sox added catcher Welington Castillo , whom Jays fans remember from his five homers against Toronto in 2017 , and the Rangers signed pitcher Doug Fister , who saw duty with the Red Sox last season . Two of the other three were career minor-leaguers signed to major-league deals . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Additionally , there were 11 players signed to minor-league deals with invitations to the big clubs&amp;rsquo ; spring training camp , and 22 players were signed to straight minor-league contracts . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Was this level of action out of the ordinary ? Let&amp;rsquo ; s check the data . The transaction data file at Retrosheet.org contains more than 88,000 moves made between December 1880 and February 2017 . True free agency didn&amp;rsquo ; t really become a factor in the majors until the reserve clause was bargained out of existence after the 1975 season following a court challenge by Curt Flood ( 1970 ) and an arbitration ruling against baseball in the cases of Andy Messersmith and Dave McNally ( 1975 ) . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Below is a chart showing the number of major-league free-agent signings by calendar week from 1976 to the opening of spring training in 2017. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;27197;TOOLONG ... class= " aligncenter size-full wp-image-77018310 " src= " https : **33;27232;TOOLONG ... alt= " " width= " 640 " height= " 485 " srcset= " https : **31;27267;TOOLONG ... 640w , https : **39;27300;TOOLONG ... 150w , https : **39;27341;TOOLONG ... 300w " sizes= " ( max-width : 640px ) 100vw , 640px " &gt;&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The data shows the peak of the free-agent season comes in week 51 after a sharp build in weeks 49 and 50 . The longer increase from the end of the post-season generally begins as early as week 43 , hitting a lower peak in week 46 and 47 before building again to the prime weeks . However , even though baseball is operating under the same basic rules since 1976 , that doesn&amp;rsquo ; t mean the current environment bears any similarity to the past . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Let&amp;rsquo ; s break it down to the last 10 seasons and see what the free-agent data shows . Below is a chart showing each week of free-agent signings from the end of the 2007 post-season to the beginning of 2017 spring training . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;27382;TOOLONG ... class= " aligncenter size-full wp-image-77018311 " src= " https : **33;27417;TOOLONG ... alt= " " width= " 640 " height= " 500 " srcset= " https : **31;27452;TOOLONG ... 640w , https : **39;27485;TOOLONG ... 150w , https : **39;27526;TOOLONG ... 300w " sizes= " ( max-width : 640px ) 100vw , 640px " &gt;&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; We see the same general shape of data with signings starting to ramp up in week 45 and the peak coming in weeks 50 and 51 . And if we zoom in on the last weeks of the year and look at the actual numbers , we can see that 2015 and 2016 have had their moves start to concentrate around week 50. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;27567;TOOLONG ... class= " aligncenter size-full wp-image-77018309 " src= " https : **33;27602;TOOLONG ... alt= " " width= " 640 " height= " 485 " srcset= " https : **31;27637;TOOLONG ... 640w , https : **39;27670;TOOLONG ... 150w , https : **39;27711;TOOLONG ... 300w " sizes= " ( max-width : 640px ) 100vw , 640px " &gt;&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; What&amp;rsquo ; s unclear from the data is whether it&amp;rsquo ; s teams or players that are driving the delay to the free-agent season . We can say that this off-season has had some unusual circumstances that may have had an impact : several teams were using resources on the chase for Shohei Ohtani ; the availability of Stanton likely delayed some decision-making on the outfield and power-hitter free agents ; and the sudden availability of the 13 international free agents stripped from the Atlanta Braves also may have drawn attention from the major-league market . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But now that Ohtani , Stanton and Kevin Maitan , the top player from the Braves investigation , have landed in their new spots , and now that the Winter Meetings are on , we ought to see a significant number of signings over the next two weeks . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Photo of the day&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; We swear there was a football game played in Buffalo yesterday afternoon . " alt= " Steel , broken from the explosions , hang from the roof after an attempted implosion of the Silverdome. " data-portal-copyright= " David Guralnick " **28;28153;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 77002327 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Silverdome was opened by the city of Pontiac in 1975 and the Lions left Tiger Stadium to play there . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Lions played in Detroit&amp;rsquo ; s northern suburb from 1975 through 2001 . At 80,300 seats for football , it was the largest facility in the league until 1997 when Washington&amp;rsquo ; s FedEx Field eclipsed it . The Silverdome also was the home of the NBA&amp;rsquo ; s Detroit Pistons from 1978-88 and the Michigan Panthers of the USFL played their two seasons there , winning the first league title in 1983. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It was the site of Super Bowl XVI between the San Francisco 49ers and Cincinnati Bengals in 1982 . In 1994 , it staged four group-stage matches in soccer&amp;rsquo ; s World Cup . The stadium drew more than 90,000 spectators for Wrestlemania III in March 1987 and for a mass by Pope John Paul II in September 1987. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The stadium was purchased at auction in 2009 by Toronto-based Triple Properties Inc . A handful of events were staged there but the stadium never found a permanent replacement tenant . Redevelopment plans never materialized . Eventually the air pressure that supported the fiberglass roof was released and the roof slowly collapsed in 2013 . The panels then tore from wind and snow damage and the stadium became a blight on the landscape . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Oakland Press &lt;a href= " http : **34;28183;TOOLONG ... rel= " noopener " target= " blank " &gt;reported&lt;/a&gt; in October that the 127-acre site is being offered for sale for about $30 million to real estate developers who would repurpose the area . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The video below offers better sound of the blasts . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;span class= " embed-youtube " style= " text-align:center ; display : block ; " &gt;&lt;iframe class='youtube-player ' type='text/html ' width= ' 640 ' height= ' 390 ' src='https : **34;28219;TOOLONG ... allowfullscreen='true ' style='border:0 ; ' **28;28255;TOOLONG ... Post Wire ServicesSun , 03 Dec 2017 19:13:35 **45;28285;TOOLONG ... your popcorn and watch Jerry Jones try to bring the NFL and Roger Goodell to heelhttp : **36;28332;TOOLONG ... src= " https : **33;28370;TOOLONG ... title= " Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones , left , stands on the field prior to his team 's game against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi 's Stadium on October 22 , 2017. " alt= " Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones , left , stands on the field prior to his team 's game against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi 's Stadium on October 22 , 2017. " data-portal-copyright= " Ezra Shaw " **28;28405;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 76966544 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; It was a lot simpler when you could just sit back and judge Jerry Jones for his avarice and his hubris . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Jones , the Dallas Cowboys&amp;rsquo ; owner , is a model villain . He built a gaudy football stadium , helped by more than US$300 million from local government , and last year opened an even-more-gaudy practice facility , complete with luxury hotel , the anticipated billion-dollar cost of which was , again , supported by funds from the local municipality and the school ( ! ) district . His ego led him to boot the exceedingly successful Jimmy Johnson from the team , and at 75 years old he continues to run the Cowboys&amp;rsquo ; football operations despite not getting to a conference finals since 1995 . He&amp;rsquo ; s downplayed football&amp;rsquo ; s brain-injury problem , sued the NFL when he didn&amp;rsquo ; t get his way on licensing deals and , notably , publicly supported the league&amp;rsquo ; s bumbling commissioner when almost no one else would . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And now it is hard not to root for him . For months Jones has been impeding the contract extension for that same commissioner , which was thought to be mostly a formality as recently as August . Roger Goodell&amp;rsquo ; s contract runs through 2019 and pays him an absurd $42 million annually , and in the late summer the league&amp;rsquo ; s owners voted &amp;mdash ; unanimously &amp;mdash ; to let a small committee work out the details of the next contract . Jones , though , flipped on Goodell , and is now said to be determined to make him take much less guaranteed money , and has threatened to sue ( again ) if his fellow owners do not agree . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This has been explained in some quarters as Jones belatedly coming to the realization that 40-something-million for a commissioner who has never handled a player-discipline matter that he couldn&amp;rsquo ; t spectacularly botch , and who is presiding over a league that is facing many serious long-term challenges , is rather too much money . But it is also plainly evident that Jones changed his mind on Goodell right about the time that the commissioner decided to suspend the Cowboys&amp;rsquo ; star running back , Ezekiel Elliott , for six games for violating the league&amp;rsquo ; s domestic-violence policy . ESPN published a report on Friday , authored by Seth Wickersham and Don Van Natta , Jr. , who holds a master&amp;rsquo ; s degree in Jerryology , that said Jones was furious about the Elliott suspension , that Goodell had assured him that the allegations of physical abuse from a former girlfriend of Elliott lacked evidence , and that Jones considered the harsh sentence against one of his best players a complete betrayal . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **33;28435;TOOLONG ... title= " NFL commissioner Roger Goodell , left and Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones in London on Nov. 9 , 2014. " alt= " NFL commissioner Roger Goodell , left and Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones in London on Nov. 9 , 2014. " data-portal-copyright= " Matt Dunham " **28;28470;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 76966545 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; And while one can certainly question the purity of Jones&amp;rsquo ; motivation &amp;mdash ; he didn&amp;rsquo ; t seem to complain much when Goodell suspended Tom Brady after one of his famously torqued investigations &amp;mdash ; it&amp;rsquo ; s also true that the man has a point : Goodell is awful at this . The Elliott case was supposed to be the test run of the NFL&amp;rsquo ; s new domestic-violence policy , which was developed after Goodell embarrassed himself and the league in the Ray Rice case . Instead of the half-assed investigation that blew up in Goodell&amp;rsquo ; s face when video evidence emerged against Rice after a light punishment , the new policy would see league investigators spend much time and money before handing the results over to Goodell for consideration . One could wonder whether sports leagues should be in the quasi-judicial investigation business at all , but at least the NFL could no longer be accused of not taking allegations against its players seriously . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And then Goodell botched the Elliott case anyway . After a year-long investigation in which the NFL&amp;rsquo ; s own lead investigator found the accuser not to be a credible witness and recommended against a suspension , Goodell ruled in the opposite direction . Rather than offer transparency , the league kept its investigators&amp;rsquo ; concerns out of the ruling , instead issuing a letter with many damning details about what Elliott is alleged to have done to the former girlfriend in the spring of 2016 . While only Elliott and his alleged victim know what truly happened , Goodell&amp;rsquo ; s handling of the case looks entirely like someone who , faced with difficult and contradictory evidence , decided he had to pick a side and then disregarded everything that might have supported the other side . It might seem unfair to the player , and through two months of appeals several courts have agreed , but this is ultimately a system in which the standard of proof is whatever the commissioner wants it to be . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It bears repeating that Jones was fine with all the other stuff that Goodell has overseen as commissioner : the foot-dragging on concussions , the shameless and dangerous move to weekly Thursday night games , the franchise relocations , the falling television ratings . Jones even played a lead role in some of that . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But if the Elliott matter , and his obvious bias in it , is the thing that finally turned Jones against Goodell , I am fine with that . Friday&amp;rsquo ; s ESPN report includes a money quote in which Jones is said to have told Goodell that he should want no part of the Wrath of Jerry . Invoking Patriots owner Robert Kraft , once displeased with the Brady suspension , Jones said : &amp;ldquo ; Bob Kraft is a p&amp;ndash ; &amp;ndash ; &amp;ndash ; y compared to what I&amp;rsquo ; m going to do . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I don&amp;rsquo ; t think he said &amp;ldquo ; party . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As that comment shows , Jones could easily alienate as many fellow owners as he brings to his side in his fight with Goodell . The prospect of a great big squabble among the NFL&amp;rsquo ; s high-and-mighty billionaires club ? In practice , this tends to mean players and coaches avoid taking a position on issues of the day , even when it falls in their lap . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **33;29875;TOOLONG ... title= " Cleveland Cavaliers forward LeBron James speaks to reporters at his team 's media day on Sept. 25. His arc &amp;mdash ; football player dies , has brain examined , is found to have signs of CTE &amp;mdash ; is utterly familiar . Many families of former players have observed behavioural changes , mental suffering that can lead to suicide , which are then explained , somewhat , by the CTE that is discovered post-mortem . Hernandez&amp;rsquo ; s lawyers will now attempt to do something unique , which is blame murderous behaviour on the damage caused by football , but it&amp;rsquo ; s of a piece with the blame placed on the sport by the families of dozens of former players who only ended up harming themselves . ( He also played in 40 games at the University of Florida . ) A pass-catching tight end , he was not the kind of player who spent long stretches bashing into opponents in the sport&amp;rsquo ; s trenches . There is no doubt that he would have taken blows to the head in his playing days , but because his career ended so early , Hernandez had simply not played that much football . When the first discoveries of CTE in former football players were made , after the alarming post-career struggles of players such as offensive lineman Mike Webster and linebacker Junior Seau , their brain damage was attributed to the years of repeated hits to their heads . @@51765558 <h> Your dollars will go to support investigative reporting that helps real people in the areas <p> As Canada 's gloomy economy hits new and historic lows due to the pandemic , the country 's infrastructure and communities minister is doubling down on her government 's equality and environmental agenda -- despite opponents ' accusations the Liberals are trying to " use this pandemic as an excuse to evade accountability " to ram through unprecedented spending . <p> Far from tightening the fiscal belt during a fiscal crisis , Catherine McKenna said her government is not going far enough , particularly in a moment when the continent is laser-focused on racial discrimination , inequality , and the health threat to the most vulnerable . <p> That 's why the minister of Infrastructure and Communities is looking to a new way of viewing what , exactly , infrastructure is : Not merely bridges , buildings and buses , but also the social institutions that have become essential during the pandemic . She called it Canada 's " social infrastructure . " <p> It could include those sectors at the pandemic front lines , for instance in health , transit and @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ most shaken by COVID-19 -- from deadly outbreaks in long-term care homes , or the education and child-care tasks that have fallen mainly on women because of the economic shutdown . <p> McKenna spoke Tuesday to Canada 's National Observer editor-in-chief Linda Solomon Wood in a wide-ranging online conversation where she spelled out why rebuilding the country 's economy after the pandemic must make this " social infrastructure " a priority -- initiatives that must include at their centre women , racialized communities , Indigenous people , and the environment . <p> One key aspect of what McKenna is reflecting on is equity , particularly around racial discrimination , she said . Specifically citing the current Black Lives Matter uprising sparked by the latest in a string of racist police killings of unarmed Black civilians , the cabinet minister and Ottawa MP said she met Tuesday night with Black leaders and advocates to learn more about how she can be part of addressing systemic racism after she signed on to a letter acknowledging its persistence in the country 's institutions . <p> " Social infrastructure has to be part of @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ need to make sure everyone is succeeding , that we 're not leaving behind Indigenous people , we need to talk to the Black community ... To order presentation-ready copies of Toronto Star content for distribution to colleagues , clients or customers , or inquire about permissions/licensing , please go to : **27;326;TOOLONG <h> Can climate capitalism cure what ails us ? Fighting climate change in the age of COVID <p> TR <p> By Tom RandCorporate Knights <p> Sat. , June 20 , 2020timer7 min. read <p> JOIN THE CONVERSATION <p> Every disaster movie starts with someone ignoring the experts . Scientists point to an impending threat with increasing alarm , but to the public the threat feels abstract , distant . Until it reaches a tipping point and suddenly everything changes . <p> Almost overnight , COVID-19 exploded from World Health Organization discussion rooms to shatter the global economy and upend our social lives . It 's an example of " systemic " risk , where nature shifts otherwise unseen boundary conditions under which we operate . Assumptions underpinning everyday security are betrayed . COVID breached an invisible line between us and pathogens . Nature 's back in the driver 's seat . We 're humbled , no longer in control . <p> @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ behaviour to limit the risk , and unlocked enormous public and private resources to resolve it . <p> Social distancing buys time . A vaccine puts the boundary back in place . Our collective response is a moral one : we took on staggering costs in the blink of an eye to protect ourselves . A united public sector is arbiter of that moral dimension . It defines the framework by which we act , and only it can provide the foundation upon which the economy recovers . <p> That unlocks a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity : as the global corporate world leans -- once again -- on the public purse for recovery , we might demand in return a renewed " climate capitalism , " a sustainable economy built for the 21st century . <p> Climate risk looks a bit like COVID-19 , if you squint . Climate risk is the mother of systemic risks . We 're changing the planetary-scale boundary conditions under which civilization evolved : the patterns of weather and water that dictate how we get our food and where we build our cities . Inaction on climate @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ response to climate risk is thus also a moral one : we act to keep ourselves safe . The public sector is director of the show , the private sector its actors . <p> COVID 's threat feels closer than climate , though -- right ? That 's why we called a political truce and acted with urgency . We want to protect our aunts , dads and friends -- today . And climate 's still way over the horizon . <p> Well ... did COVID feel so immediate a few months ago ? The risk of a pandemic was always there ; we just ignored it . And the climate threat feels less distant with each new firestorm , flood or drought . Ask an Australian how up close and personal climate risk feels , or someone whose home burned in Fort McMurray or California . A new generation , led by Greta Thunberg , certainly feels an immediate sense of insecurity . <p> There 's one crucial difference no amount of squinting can reconcile . Worst case on COVID is we screw up on social distancing but still @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ along . We can fail on COVID and recover . Failure on climate is forever . There 's no putting planetary boundaries back once they shift to more energetic and dangerous states . It 's a one-way trip . There 's no equivalent of social distancing to buy time , marshal resources and plan a counterattack . So we have to invent a vaccine in advance . That 's climate capitalism : a vaccine to anticipate climate risk . <p> Left and right united under COVID -- Trudeau and Ford working together ! -- because people wo n't tolerate leadership that ca n't protect them , whatever their political stripes . You do n't have to be a lefty to appreciate a strong public sector today . Neither must you be a Wall Street titan to understand market forces ; big corporations and private capital are powerful tools to solve wicked problems -- if given focus . We see that with COVID : the private sector scales up needed tech -- tests , vaccines , treatments -- when co-ordinated and incented by the public sector . Climate capitalism is no @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ on climate but only when incented and directed by an empowered and united public sector . <p> But on climate the political divide grows wider . Many on the far left -- led by Naomi Klein -- blame capitalism itself for climate risk and would have us throw it out . <p> This is misguided in three ways . First , we ca n't possibly rebuild energy systems without private capital , innovation and all the complex activity only markets can organize . Greenhouse gases are n't DDT ; you ca n't just ban them . Second , radicalizing the politics of climate hinders the work of building the large tent needed for decisive action in a democracy . Third , it sets arbitrary limits on what capitalism can look like . If Klein 's target was limited to American-style , free-market fundamentalism , she 'd have many allies , including me . <p> On the other side of this cultural divide sit reasonable people , civic and business leaders who understand that climate risk is real but prefer an incremental approach . They fear radical intervention in the economy @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ edges . That too is misguided : a bit like lifting COVID 's social distancing restrictions too soon because you fear short-term pain . The reduction in risk is illusory . It 's the long game that matters . It 's too late to nibble around the edges ; only deep , radical cuts in emissions will do . Incrementalism feeds into Klein 's radical narrative : " See ? Capitalists wo n't do what 's necessary . Let 's bring it all down ! " <p> Capitalism is n't monolithic . It means different things to different people . For an ordinary person , it might mean owning your own bakery , working for options in a tech start-up or watching your RRSP grow so you can retire in comfort . It can mean Russia 's anarcho-capitalism , Indonesia 's crony capitalism or China 's state capitalism . Sweden is as much a capitalist country , in this view , as America . There 's no preordained role for the public sector . Roosevelt 's New Deal did n't make the U.S. any less capitalist . Nor is private @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ citizens endorse . There 's no predetermined moral dimension : it 's neither good nor bad , but reflects human complexity . <p> Climate capitalism is a rewiring of the economy using whatever works to put a cork in emissions -- whether they come from the left , right or anywhere else . Economic radicalism is not the same thing as political radicalism . We harness as many existing institutions as possible for the sake of expediency . We do n't throw out the machinery of capitalism ; we replace the fuel . <p> Twenty years ago , the story would start and end here : price carbon -- start low , ratchet it up slowly , keep it revenue-neutral so it 's not a government cash grab . Sit back and watch the market work its magic . Optimally efficient , it 's the incrementalist 's dream ! Unfortunately , it 's too late for that soft landing . If your house is on fire , you do n't care if the hose leaks ; you just want lots of water . Speed matters more than efficiency . <p> @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ . Here are some ideas . <p> Has anyone fought an election over efficiency regulations ? Car mileage standards or the carbon content of fuel ? Sustainable energy professor Mark Jaccard points out that the heavy lifting on emissions reductions thus far , whether in Canada or California , was borne by regulations . Many define an outcome -- say , energy use in buildings -- without defining how to get there . Jaccard calls them " flex-regs . " Fast , effective , often under the political radar . <p> Remember " Own the Podium " back in the Vancouver Olympics ? We picked athletes who competed at an international level and gave them resources to train . Do the same for cleantech . Back companies with demonstrated traction in global markets with loan guarantees for production and project finance . Today , old stuff gets cheap capital , new tech does n't . Let 's flip that around . This is n't the government picking winners ; it 's the government backing winners -- a big difference . <h> Get the latest in your inbox <p> Never miss @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ coverage , with our email newsletters <p> Teach young CFOs that energy costs are of strategic importance . Why ? Because capital budgets are reserved for core investments : more T-shirt machines for a T-shirt company , bigger holes in the ground if you 're a miner . Energy retrofits are stuck begging from operating budgets , which means they need paybacks in a year or so . Most efficiency fruit remains unpicked , across the economy . Yet rare is the CFO who gets more than 15 to 20 per cent on core capital and efficiency pays twice that ! No policy required , just fresh thinking . <p> Fund low-carbon infrastructure with green bonds , with a twist . The government raises cheap capital with a Canada Savings Bond-like instrument . The private sector bids on the right to deploy it . A public mandate incents those private money managers with a single metric : maximize carbon reduction at minimum cost to Joe Public . A green bank , done right , combines the public cost of capital with the private sector 's nose for profit . <p> @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ We gave up a degree of sovereignty to the World Trade Organization . It has real teeth that impinge upon national governments . Leverage those teeth . The WTO ( and World Bank and International Monetary Fund ) reflects the priorities of those who negotiated it . If Trump can upend NATO , imagine how an empowered group of national leaders might reform the WTO to level the playing field between countries by forcing climate laggards to bear carbon tariffs . <p> Nothing can redeem COVID . It 's a nasty little thing . But maybe it 'll help us hear experts on climate risk and reconcile the priority of long-term stability over short-term cost . We might also use the strongest public hand we 've had in a long time and write a new climate contract between citizens , our governments and the private sector . If so , we 'll emerge the stronger for COVID , however horrid its impacts . <p> Tom Rand is a cleantech investor and author of " The Case for Climate Capitalism : Economic Solutions for a Planet in Crisis .
